articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Doherty-mode OLMBA for Enhanced Back-Off Efficiency Over an Octave Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper presents a new design for the OLMBA focused on exploiting a Doherty-like mode with one device in class AB and the other in class C to enhance 6 dB output back-off efficiency across an octave bandwidth of 0.8 to 1.6 GHz. The simulation results show that the device can achieve 48 to 53 % back-off PAE while delivering an output power of 46 to 48 dBm at 3 dB compression and 12.6 to 16.1 dB gain. Furthermore, the operation of this device seems to conform with the operation of Doherty power amplifiers in terms of how the intrinsic impedance changes between back-off and saturation. Whilst this is only based on simulated results, it does show that it is a promising design for a high-efficiency, wide-bandwidth OLMBA for linear applications.

articleTitle: Characterization Procedure for Effective Evaluation of III-V Compound Semiconductor Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: In this paper, a characterization procedure for III-V compound semiconductor technology is proposed, with the aim of investigating the performance of state-of-the-art transistors for mm-wave applications. The whole procedure has been successfully applied to a 0.1-µm GaAs pHEMT process, which was characterized under DC, small- and large-signal operations, after a first stress experiment necessary to assess its robustness and stability.

articleTitle: A 10 W C-Ku Band MMIC NDPA for Electronic Warfare Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper presents a C-Ku band Non-Uniform Distributed Power Amplifier (NDPA) operating between 4 – 18 GHz. The challenging design approach aims to optimize the gain-bandwidth (GBW) product, providing a remarkable average output power above 10 W with an associated average power added efficiency (PAE) equal to 18.5 % over the entire operative range of frequencies. The NDPA provides also a challenging average linear gain of 14.5 dB with a marked corresponding gain-bandwidth product when compared to the state of the art. The MMIC NDPA has been designed and fabricated using 0.25 µm AlGaN/GaN HEMT process provided by Leonardo foundry.

articleTitle: Towards Quantifying Two-Mode Correlation Linewidths in Quantum Circuits
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper aims to quantify the linewidth of two-mode correlations in Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifiers (TWPAs). Artifacts induced by data acquisition and processing, such as windowing effects and acquisition time, are examined to understand their influence on the linewidth estimation of these correlations. The findings underscore the significance of acquisition parameters in optimizing two-mode correlation measurements, enhancing device characterization for quantum applications.

articleTitle: A Ku-band GaN PA with GaAs Gate Modulator for Improved Linearity
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: A Ku-Band GaN power amplifier (PA) and a GaAs gate modulator are presented. The MMICs work together to amplify signals efficiently while maintaining linearity via gate modulation. In particular, the GaN PA demonstrates a power added efficiency (PAE) greater than 30 %, more than 2W of output power, and a large-signal gain exceeding 13 dB from 11–16 GHz. The gate modulator is designed to extract envelopes with instantaneous bandwidths up to 2 GHz and is measured with a 20MHz LTE signal as well as 2-tone signals with bandwidths up to 800 MHz. The measured PA data is used in an envelope simulator to show IMD3 better than 35 dBc at $\overline {{{\mathbf{P}}_{{\text{out }}}}} = 30{\text{dBm}}$ with gate modulation for a 100MHz 2-tone signal. This represents a 20 dB improvement in IMD3 compared to the static bias case.

articleTitle: Tunable Inductive Output Matching for W-Band Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive inductive matching approach using tunable transmission lines in SiGe BiCMOS technology to improve power amplifier (PA) performance in mmWave applications. By varying the tuning voltage, the effective inductance and impedance of the lines can be adjusted, enhancing the PA’s adaptability to changing conditions. Simulations and S-parameter measurements validate the concept, showing significant impedance changes. Implementing this in a W-band PA demonstrates improved performance over 75 to 90 GHz. Notably, output power and power-added efficiency (PAE) were optimized, achieving 13.9 dBm and 13.9% PAE at 75 GHz, and 9.3% PAE at 90 GHz. These results highlight the potential of adaptive matching for advanced PA designs in high-frequency applications.

articleTitle: Assessment of Dynamic Deviation Reduction-Based Volterra Modeling and Digital Predistortion of RF Passive Doubler
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) multipliers (FreqXs) are promising devices for wideband signal generation, as they eliminate the need for a local oscillator (LO) and can operate with wide signal bandwidths (BWs). However, modeling and linearization tools specifically designed for FreqXs are essential to accurately describe and compensate for their inherent nonlinear behavior. In this paper, the dynamic-deviation reduction (DDR) Volterra modeling approach is applied to an off-the-shelf frequency doubler. The experiments are conducted using a vector network analyzer (VNA) equipped with modern signal analysis, which allowed to extract and validate the cross-harmonic DDR model at 39 GHz output carrier frequency. Finally, DDR-based digital predistortion (DPD) reached unequalized error vector magnitude (EVM) down to less than 5% for a 256-QAM modulation with 100-MHz BW.

articleTitle: On the Implementation of Capacitance Models in Electronic Computer-Aided Design Tools
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: Different types of CAD capacitance implementation procedures are discussed: Capacitance, Charge, Total charge, and Charge–Current. The last two models are now implemented and available in commercial CAD tools ADS and Cadence.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient and Linearity-Enhanced S-band Doherty Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This work presents the design and characterization of a hybrid Doherty power amplifier for S band aiming at enhancing linearity near saturation while maintaining high efficiency. The design combines two highly linear branch amplifiers in a Doherty configuration through a quadrature coupler with reactive termination at the isolated port. At 2.7GHz, the amplifier demonstrates 13.9dB small signal gain, 41dBm saturated power, and 67% maximum efficiency. The linearity is evaluated through two-tone and modulated signal characterizations, showing -30dBc IMD3 up to 36dBm of output power. Additionally, the ACPR is -30dBc and -39dBc, respectively, before and after digital predistortion.

articleTitle: Load/Source-Pull Evaluation of Modulated Performance in GaAs HBT Power Cells for WiFi-6
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)

articleTitle: Non-linear Microwave Transistor Modeling through ANNs: a Frequency-domain CAD Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This contribution presents a black-box approach based on Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) for the accurate and computationally efficient non-linear modeling of microwave transistors. The presented model, here applied to a MESFET test-case, adopts a feed-forward ANN to relate the harmonic components of the device’s incident and reflected port waves with arbitrary harmonic loading. As such, it is conceived to be exploited for non-linear design within RF CAD tools based on the Harmonic Balance approach. The detailed implementation within Keysight Advance Design System (ADS), resorting to built-in custom modeling features, is also presented along with model validation results, demonstrating the potential of the proposed approach for fully-black-box non-linear device modeling.

articleTitle: A Knowledge-Based Transfer Learning Capacitance Model for GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: ANN models are highly data-dependent, particularly requiring dense multi-bias S-parameter measurements to capture the bias dependency of capacitance-voltage (C-V) models. This requirement can be costly. To address this issue, we propose a transfer-learning-assisted method aimed at reducing the number of S-parameter measurements. Initially, a feature extractor is developed to capture the bias dependency of the capacitance model using simulations. Then, for new devices from different process (e.g., different gate length and threshold voltage), the knowledge of feature extractor is then integrated with a capacitance regressor to construct the C-V model. Validation results demonstrate that while the proposed method and traditional ANN models exhibit comparable accuracy in both small-signal and large-signal performance, the traditional ANN model requires six times more measured S-parameters for model construction compared to the proposed method

articleTitle: Optimization Methodology for Wideband SLMBA Design Considering Balanced Amplifiers’ Off-State Impedance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This work proposes an optimization design methodology considering the balanced amplifiers’ (BAs) off-state impedance in wideband sequential load-modulated balanced amplifiers (SLMBA) design. The detailed design process is outlined, and the proposed method effectively mitigates the efficiency degradation in the back-off region caused by the non-infinite BAs’ off-state impedance under wideband operation. A 1.6 to 2.7 GHz SLMBA with a 10-dB OBO was implemented to validate the design. The fabricated SLMBA achieved a peak output power of 47.9-49.1 dBm, with a corresponding drain efficiency (DE) of 60.1%-67.5% and a DE of 44.5%-60.2% at 10 dB OBO over a 51.2% fractional bandwidth (FBW). These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design method.

articleTitle: A Behavioral Approach to Equivalent-Circuit Modeling of GaN MMIC Varactor Cells
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: A measurement-based, nonlinear modeling approach for Microwave Monolithic Integrated Circuit (MMIC) varactor cells is proposed. The technique exploits the combination of the vector fitting (VF) algorithm and the Bott-Duffin (BD) network synthesis to automatically yield an equivalent-circuit model from multibias S-parameters measurements. The method is validated for three varactor cells with different layout features.

articleTitle: A GaN-on-SiC Transmit/Receive MMIC Frontend for 6-to-18-GHz Phased Array Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This work presents a monolithic transmit/receive (T/R) frontend for the 6–18-GHz band, implemented in 150-nm gallium-nitride (GaN) technology. Single-die integration is leveraged by co-designing all subcircuits: the T/R asymmetric switch simplifies the transmit (Tx) path to save for Tx output power and efficiency, while its receive (Rx) branch merges into the low-noise amplifier input matching network for compactness and reduced noise. On-wafer measurements show an average Tx output power of 9.5 W (minimum 5.6 W) with 19.4% efficiency (minimum 13.5%) across the band. In Rx mode, the prototypes exhibit over 21 dB gain with an average noise figure of 3 dB (maximum 3.3 dB). These metrics compete with the state of the art of ultrawideband GaN-based single-chip T/R frontends.

articleTitle: Temperature-Dependent Vector-Calibrated Large-Signal Measurements of a GaN-Based SPDT Ka-Band Switch
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper reports temperature-dependent small-and large-signal measurements of a 32 – 38 GHz GaN-based SPDT switch MMIC which employs a double shunt topology and is designed into a 140 nm GaN HEMT process. The switch MMIC exhibits 1.23 – 1.5 dB insertion loss, >25.8 dB isolation, and a 1 dB compression > 31 dBm. The switch MMIC is also characterized at higher ambient temperatures, and the rate of change versus temperature for several switch figures of merit are reported. This work could provide important data for circuit designers to project switch MMIC performance to high temperatures.

articleTitle: A Two-Octave GaN Power Amplifier based on a Multi-Section Chebyshev Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and characterization of an ultra-wideband (0.8GHz–3.2GHz) hybrid single-stage class-AB power amplifier based on a 25-W packaged GaN device. Over this two-octave bandwidth, the amplifier reaches saturated output power higher than 42dBm with associated efficiency above 53%. An output matching network consisting of a 4section Chebyshev transformer has been implemented based on the optimum load trajectory, targeting a trade-off between output power and efficiency.

articleTitle: Fast Optimization of RF Power Transistors with mmWave Active Load-Pull Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: The paper presents a peak-search method for active continuous wave (CW) load-pull measurements for implementation in an autonomous characterization system aimed at optimizing mmWave RF power transistors. The approach utilizes a downhill simplex algorithm to find a target impedance or to determine the optimal output impedances to achieve maximum output power or power added efficiency (PAE) in a load-pull system based on open-loop active injection. An 8-term error model with power calibration, based on large signal vector network analyzer (LSNA) equations is implemented, to ensure highly accurate measurements for the wave correction. The downhill simplex algorithm demonstrates excellent repeatability and robustness with a std of 0.08 dB in the output power over ten measurements and Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">load</inf> std of 0.02 in magnitude and 1.78° in phase. It is shown to accurately identify the target load impedances while maintaining a fast convergence.

articleTitle: A 10 W GaN/Si Doherty Power Amplifier Designed for 15 GHz 6G Band with 8 dB Backoff Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a 10W GaN-on-Si Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) for operation in the 15 GHz 6G band. The DPA was fabricated using Infineon’s RF GaN-on-Si MMIC process. An experimental (simulation) result shows a peak PAE of 30–37%, and 22–27% PAE at 8 dB backoff, 10dB gain, and 2 GHz bandwidth. Thermally limited CW measurements confirmed high back-off efficiency with 24% PAE at 29 dBm output power at 14 GHz.

articleTitle: Exploring Software-Defined Radio Based Noise Measurementes: Perfomances Analysis and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: In this paper for the first time an experimental investigation on the use of a software-defined radio (SDR) for radio-frequency noise measurements is performed. After the characterization of radio-frequency key parameters, the stability of noise measurements was also studied by exploiting the Allan variance. The comprehensive characterization based on SDRs, makes it possible to notify how different operational settings may affect the achievable measurements performance.

articleTitle: An example of the role of time-modulated capacitances in microwave time-varying systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: Time-varying systems enable advanced electromagnetic devices by surpassing the limitations of conventional designs. This paper presents the influence of the time-modulation shape on an example of a time-varying system. The circuit is a coupled-resonator filter which is already available in the literature and which presents non-reciprocal frequency behaviour due to the time modulation of its capacitances. Different modulation schemes, including sinusoidal and sawtooth signals, are evaluated through MATLAB simulations to assess the effects of non-linear varactor C-V characteristic and other modulation specifications on filter performance. It is verified that the fundamental parameters that control the frequency response are the modulation period and the relative amplitude of the time variation. The specific shape of the modulation (i.e., its higher harmonics) seems to play a secondary role in the studied cases.

articleTitle: Automated On-Wafer Radio-Frequency Transistor Characterization with Adaptive Probing and Features Extraction with Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper describes an autonomous on-wafer S-parameter and DC measurement system for radio frequency (RF) power transistors with an adaptive probing algorithm. The Devices Under Test (DUTs) are measured in the small signal domain up to 40 GHz. DC and RF features are extracted, together with their derived uncertainties. The DUTs are contacted with an improved adaptive probing method, enabling a precise touch-down of the probes on the structures’ pads. To show the capabilities of the system, Gallium Nitride (GaN) High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) on a GaN on SiC wafer were measured, together with their respective de-embedding structures. The system enables the statistical evaluation of the HEMTs’ features mapped as the spread in performance over the wafer which is here exemplified by presenting their extracted threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>), the transient frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>) and the maximum oscillation frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf>). The uncertainty in the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf> is on average 30 mV in the central shots. The novel adaptive probing algorithm reduces the skating precision and accuracy error from 3 µm to 1 µm and is shown to improve the uncertainty of the extracted f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf> by around 70%.

articleTitle: Enhancement of mmW Detection Using Dual-Terminal Excitation in Transistors
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This work investigates the potential use of a GaN based HEMT as a millimeter-wave band detector by optimizing the excitation scheme through simultaneous signal injection at the gate and drain terminals. By implementing a dual-terminal excitation scheme, with synchronous signal injection at the gate and drain ports, we achieved a significant enhancement in current responsivity compared to conventional single-terminal excitation. Experimental results show a two-fold (2x) improvement in responsivity by optimizing the amplitude ratio and phase shift between the injected signals. These findings establish GaN HEMTs as promising candidates for high-performance RF detection in applications such as wireless communication and sensing.

articleTitle: Digital Self-Interference Cancellation for In-Band Full-Duplex Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper introduces a digital self-interference cancellation (SIC) technique for an in-band full-duplex (IBFD) system. The SIC approach relies in the estimation of the selfinterference signal by using a generalized memory polynomial behavioral model with Ito-Hermite orthogonal polynomials. The effectiveness of the proposed digital SIC approach is validated by considering two types of channels, an additive white gaussian noise (AWGN) and an extended vehicular activities (EVA) channel, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a 3.5 GHz Symmetric Doherty PA in an 8-inch GaN on Silicon MMIC Technology for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This work discusses the design of a symmetric single-stage DPA MMIC, employing a novel 8-inch GaN on silicon-based MMIC technology. Leveraging, the high gain of the 250 nm AlGaN/GaN HEMT, the proposed Doherty amplifier provides 10 W of output power around the frequency of 3.5 GHz with a single stage. This work uses a lumped element approach to minimises losses due to the conductive substrate and additionally reduces the required area of the amplifier that occupies 13.68 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of space. From measurements, it is seen that the presented amplifier exhibits a large signal gain of 16.7 dB, a peak drain efficiency greater than 60% and a -6 dB back-off efficiency of 48% between 3.5 GHz to 3.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-Octave RF PA based on PSO method with Individually Self-Adaptive Hyperparameters
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: With the increasing demand for high-performance power amplifiers (PA) in modern wireless systems, PA design has become ever more complex, making PA optimization extremely challenging. This paper proposes a particle swarm optimization algorithm with individually self-adaptive hyperparameters (PSO-ISH), which can enable more efficient optimization. A high-performance multi-octave PA with 10-W gallium nitride (GaN) transistors has been developed to validate the proposed strategy. This PA can reach a power added efficiency (PAE) of greater than 58%, an output power of greater than 40 dBm, and a gain of greater than 10 dB in the 0.6GHz-4GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: A Design Method for Wide Bandwidth Reflective Analog Predistorters
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This work proposes a design method for broadband reflection type analog predistorters (APD). It is composed of a 90° hybrid coupler loaded with equal variable reflection coefficient in the thru and coupled ports, obtained through dedicated matching networks (MN) that adjust the nonlinear device response to the target impedance profile, obtaining the desired AM/AM or AM/PM curves. Knowing that in a lossless two-port MN, the VSWR in both ports is unchanged, and taking advantage of the fact that the MN’s group delay is arbitrary, an APD with a specific nonlinear characteristic can be obtained over a broadband frequency range, practically limited by the hybrid coupler bandwidth. A broadband APD (1.4-2 GHz) is designed to linearize a 10W GaN HEMT PA, resulting in an ACLR improvement of 7-13 dB.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Trapping Dynamics in GaN HEMTs from Double-Pulse RF Load-Pull Measurements
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This study presents the application of a recently proposed double-pulsed radio-frequency (RF) measurement technique for characterizing the dynamic behavior of Gallium Nitride (GaN) High-Electron-Mobility Transistors (HEMTs). In particular, the measurement procedure aims to analyze the trapping and detrapping mechanisms affecting the device’s performance under realistic RF operating conditions. By varying both the RF prepulse duration and the time interval between the RF prepulse and the main RF pulse (ranging from a few microseconds to a few milliseconds), a wide range of trap capture and release dynamics can be evaluated.

Index Terms: Gallium Nitride High Electron Mobility Transistors

articleTitle: A Simple Lumped-Element Topology for Wideband Class-E Operation at UHF and L Bands
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: In this paper, a lumped-element circuit topology is presented for approximating class-E operation along a wide frequency range. Exploiting the design space offered by the generalization or continuum of class-E equations, a dc-feed coil and a simple doubly resonant output network may provide the required terminating conditions for a high-efficiency and nearly constant output power amplifier operation over a significant fractional bandwidth. The topology is insensitive to resistive load variations at the central frequency, of potential interest for its use in load modulation (LM) transmitter architectures among other applications. Two GaN HEMT power amplifiers have been designed and characterized at UHF and L bands. The measured efficiency is above 75%, from 625 MHz to 1025 MHz and from 1.075 GHz to 1.375 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency C/X Dual-Band HPA in 250-nm Gate Length GaN HEMT Technology with 10W Pout
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper describes a dual-band (C/X) high power amplifier realised with Leonardo's 0.25 μm GaN on SiC technology. Design considerations are provided to implement dual-band operation. The measured data show PAE values in excess of 50% in both bands with an output power greater than 10 W. The results compare very well with the open literature, especially in terms of PAE.

articleTitle: A 10 W Ultra-Wideband MMIC HPA for EW Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband High Power Amplifier (HPA) operating in the 6-18 GHz frequency range. The design approach tackles the challenge of achieving an average output power equal to 10 W under 20-V VDD power supply, with over 24.5 dB power gain and an associated Power Added Efficiency (PAE) of over 28% across the entire operational frequency range. The HPA delivers an average linear gain of 35 dB, outperforming current state-of-the-art solutions. The MMIC HPA has been designed and fabricated using 0.15 µm AlGaN/GaN HEMT process provided by the UMS foundry.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of VSWR-Adaptive Balanced Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper reports on the characterization procedure and the measurement results of a modified balanced power amplifier architecture that enables an adaptative Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) protection. Implementation of a Sband power amplifier demonstrator with commercially available components (power amplifiers, quadrature hybrid couplers and variable attenuators) is proposed. The principle of the modified balanced power amplifier architecture as well as the strategy followed to control the input signal level as function of the targeted maximum VSWR is presented and discussed. In a first step a test set-up based on the use of a 4-port PNA-X and Arduino Mega is described to validate the operation principle of the demonstrator. Continuous Wave (CW) measurements in the 1-3GHz frequency band are presented with different load mismatch conditions. In a second step, an analog implementation of VSWR detection and feedback loop circuitry is proposed. A dedicated test bench based on the use of a two channel RF Vector Signal Generator (VSG) will be used for the dynamic characterization of the proposed demonstrator.

articleTitle: A PA Model for Fast Linearity and Efficiency Evaluation under Modulated Signal Excitations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper presents a behavioral model for predicting the linearity and efficiency of RF power amplifiers (PAs) under modulated signal excitations. The model is constructed using continuous wave (CW) data collected across various input amplitudes and frequencies, capturing both RF and DC characteristics of the PA. The measured data enables the estimation of amplifier performance, including power, linearity, and efficiency, when excited by modulated signals. The proposed approach is validated for a single ended and Doherty PA in simulation, built at different operation frequencies and using different devices; and for a single-ended PA in measurement; using OFDM signals with bandwidths up to 100MHz for both simulations and measurement tests. This method provides a streamlined and effective tool for both design-stage optimization and post-manufacturing system simulations.

articleTitle: Temperature and Concentration Retrieval in Microwave Dielectric Spectroscopy using a Two-Tier Machine Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: Precise dielectric characterization of materials through concentration and temperature analysis is an essential yet challenging process due to the strong dependency of permittivity on both parameters. Polar materials such as aqueous solutions are particularly more prone to permittivity variation under different chemical or physical conditions, making it difficult to distinguish between samples with similar permittivity values at varying concentrations and temperatures. Thus, in this work, we employ data processing together with a two-tier machine learning framework to recognize the intricate differences of mixtures with 0 to 90% ethanol content measured at different temperatures. The first tier is the K-nearest neighbor (KNN) classifier for temperature while the second one is a neural network regressor to estimate concentration. Through proper feature engineering and selection, we achieved a high accuracy of 99.65% for the first tier, which ultimately contributed to the high overall accuracy of 99.45% achieved using the combined framework.

articleTitle: MMIC Power Amplifier in GaAs HBT Technology for Wi-Fi 6 Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This contribution presents a 3.5W MMIC power amplifier in GaAs HBT technology operating at 5 V supply conceived for Wi-Fi 6 applications in the 5-6 GHz frequency range. A 3-stage corporate architecture is selected to evaluate the technology capability in terms of power, linearity and efficiency. In simulation, the designed amplifier shows a saturated output power in excess of 35 dBm with associated gain and efficiency above 27 dB and 36 %, respectively. At -26 dB of EVM (Error Vector Magnitude, MCS0 standard) the best efficiency achievable, with simple bias tuning, is 17 % with an associated output power of 29 dBm. The small-signal characterization shows a very good agreement between measurements and simulations.

articleTitle: Cardiff Behavioral Model of a Ka-Band SPDT Switch Trained on Structured Minimization of Load-Pull Characterization Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the Cardiff behavioral model based on the large-signal response of a single pole, double throw switch (SPDT) to realize a tunable reactive termination for advanced power amplifier architectures operating in the Ka-band up to 3 watts. The model was developed using a comprehensive load-pull (LP) characterization dataset comprising 2176 data points. Subsequently, it was trained to replicate this dataset with only 44 input data points, achieving an acceptable accuracy reflected by an NMSE of -33.8 dB.

articleTitle: Sparse Volterra-Based Models for I/Q Impairments and Nonlinear Distortion of Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: An overview of sparse Volterra-based models for wideband power amplifiers is presented in an easy-to-understand way, by means of sample code for a set of examples. It is shown how the regressors structure of a properly selected Volterra-based model, together with the use of sparse regression techniques to reduce the number of active components, provide accurate representations of both I/Q impairments and nonlinear distortion.

articleTitle: A 200/400 GHz Cascode SiGe Voltage-Controlled Oscillator Exploiting Harmonic Optimization Technique for mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This brief presents a Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) for operation in the mmWave frequency range. The VCO is based on the Colpitts topology, utilising SiGe:C 130 nm bipolar devices. Unlike traditional configurations, the proposed VCO simultaneously provides both a differential output at the fundamental frequency (200 GHz) and a push-push output at the second harmonic (400 GHz). The overall performance is significantly enhanced through the implementation of an innovative Second Harmonic Extraction Network (SHEN), which efficiently captures and utilizes the second harmonic for improved output power and efficiency.

articleTitle: Improved Iterative Envelope Simulation for the Efficient Prediction of the Impact of Wideband Modulated Signals on Power Amplifier Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: A previously introduced Iterative Envelope Simulator is expanded upon. The new implementation uses a Matlab-controlled ADS circuit simulator, allowing for the simulation of manufacturer provided nonlinear transistor models. The model is validated with 2-tone and 256-Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (256-QAM) stimuli applied to a power amplifier with a resonant BB network. Its output is compared against 2-tone HB simulations and ADS envelope simulations. The 2-tone results show that the improved simulation captures the same trend as the HB simulator. The new model introduces the ability to predict signal linearity for complex signal modulation schemes. It is capable of predicting the issues related to the resonant networks for the 256-QAM signal, showing a significant Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) degradation when the signal envelope starts overlapping the resonant frequency, while the traditional envelope simulator does not capture this issue.

articleTitle: Analysis and Development of a Two RF Input Load Modulated Envelope Tracking PA
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This work introduces the load-modulation technique to improve the power handling capabilities of envelope tracking (ET) power amplifiers. It is based on an auxiliary amplifier capable to inject at the main amplifier output terminal a copy of its input signal, properly phased and scaled in magnitude. By this approach, the ET output termination can track the bias supply thus maintaining the maximum dynamics of both current and voltage at the device output terminal. The proposed load-modulated envelope tracking (LM-ET) is demonstrated through the design analysis, and the development of a prototype characterized in the 3600 – 3800 MHz frequency bandwidth. Experimental results demonstrate an improvement of 3 dB at 5 dB power back-off maintaining the overall efficiency degradation of maximum 9%.

Author Keywords: gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor

articleTitle: Transformer Based Waveform Engineered Power Amplifier in a 65 nm Bulk-CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper presents a tuned transformer-based waveform-engineered power amplifier (PA). A two-stage PA is designed and fabricated in a 65 nm bulk CMOS process. A 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order transformer-based compact output network co-designed with the PA parasitics has been implemented to provide harmonic termination to the PA and improve the bandwidth. In addition, the amplifier is designed to have a class-J-like waveform to achieve both linearity and efficiency. The PA achieves a bandwidth from 5.7 to 7.9 GHz with a peak saturated power of 16 dBm and a peak efficiency of 21 % at 1.2 V. The designed PA has the capability to work from a supply voltage of 1.2 V to 0.6 V. Output power of 10 dBm (6 dB back-off) with a peak efficiency of 13 % is achieved at 0.7 V supply. At 0.6 V, the PA has an output power of 7.5 dBm with an efficiency of 10 %. The PA achieves an IMD3 of -28 dBc at 7.5 GHz for a supply of 1 V.

articleTitle: Impact of Incomplete Conversion Data Extraction on Large-Signal Stability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This contribution provides, by means of a simple, applied example, a quick recapitulation of the conversion matrix-related theory behind the stability analysis of electronic circuits under large-signal, periodic excitations. In particular, it is recalled that some level of approximation is inherent to the conversion matrix representation of the circuit as soon as a finite harmonic order is assumed. However, better and better accuracy of the representation (and therefore reliability of the tests based on that) ensues with increasing the harmonic order. On the other hand, it is shown that purposely neglecting the trans-frequential elements of the conversion matrix representation is not justified and leads in general to unreliable results.

articleTitle: Characterization and Modeling of Dual-Input Doherty Power Amplifier for High Efficiency and Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper presents the improvement, in terms of efficiency, that can be achieved by a dual-input Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) in relation to the more classical single-input configuration. The better results obtained from the dual-input solution are intrinsically connected to the independent control of the two inputs in terms of power and phase. In particular, above the power backoff point, the degree of freedom given by the control of the phase difference between the inputs allows one to operate in a condition of maximum efficiency at any output power level. To test the board and validate the results, a dedicated experimental setup for the characterization of the amplifier has been designed and realized. As will be demonstrated, the efficiency of a dual-input DPA is considerably improved compared to the single-input configuration.

articleTitle: Impact on Linearity of a Wideband Design Strategy for an Integrated GaN Doherty Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2025 International Workshop on Integrated Nonlinear Microwave and Millimetre-Wave Circuits (INMMIC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and linearity characterization of an integrated Doherty amplifier for 5G applications in the FR1 bands, implemented on a 150 nm GaN/SiC HEMT technology. It achieves 5G real-case-scenario performance over a 41% state-of-the-art fractional bandwidth, with 37 dBm saturated output power, 19 dB small-signal gain, and power-added efficiency above 20% over 6 dB back-off. The impact of the wideband combiner strategy on the linearity of the amplifier is analyzed in terms of baseband impedance and AM/PM. The characterization is then presented, with continuous wave and modulated signals for 100 MHz and 200 MHz instantaneous bandwidths. In presence of a 256-QAM 200 MHz input signal, the predistorted amplifier presents at 4.15 GHz an EVM of 2.9%.
